diagnosis: All four rollouts revealed both PF1 and PF2 and cited them in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy problems. The gate failed because three checks are overly sensitive to natural paraphrasing in the settlement's commitment structure and reference_type wording. C8 (linked to PF1) failed only in rollout 0, where the model bundled the financial terms into a single commitment of type "financial" instead of splitting them into separate "wage_payment" and "general_release" commitments as rollouts 1–3 did. C9 (linked to PF2) failed only in rollout 0, where the model used commitment types "reference" and "rehire_status" instead of the "neutral_reference" and "rehire_eligibility" types that rollouts 1–3 used. C6 (linked to PF2) failed in rollouts 2 and 3 because the reference_type field was paraphrased — rollout 2 wrote "dates of employment, job title" and rollout 3 wrote "covering dates, title" instead of the exact phrase "stating only dates, title" that C6 apparently requires. All failures are ENCODING MISMATCH: the facts were revealed and cited, but the checks' thresholds do not accommodate natural variation in how models encode the same information.
